quotes.text: When you buy through a CSP partner, Microsoft is not your billing contact. The partner handles billing, support, and provisioning.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Explains the core shift in responsibility under CSP.

quotes.text: The partner earns the margin on the service layer, not the software. That's the model. The license gets you in the door. The services keep you there.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Memorable summary of how CSP partners actually make money.

quotes.text: The practical impact is simple. Plan your headcount carefully before buying. If you are unsure, it is safer to over buy slightly than to under buy.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Actionable advice given NCE's ban on mid-term seat reductions.

quotes.text: CSP is not a discount program. It's a service delivery program. The discount doesn't come from Microsoft. It comes from the partner's service.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Corrects a widespread misconception about CSP.

quotes.text: The tradeoff is simple. CSP for flexibility and support, EA for the lowest price at scale.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: A crisp decision rule between CSP and an Enterprise Agreement.

Why customers choose a CSP partner

takeaways: The Cloud Solution Provider program lets partners resell Microsoft cloud services and own billing, support and provisioning for their customers.
Under the new commerce experience, monthly, annual and triennial terms carry different prices, and seats can be added but not reduced after the short cancellation window.
CSP is a service delivery program rather than a discount program: it suits small and mid-sized businesses, while large, stable organizations should compare it with an Enterprise Agreement.
hook: Most businesses buying Microsoft 365 or Azure through a partner are already using CSP without knowing how it works. This episode explains the Cloud Solution Provider program for IT buyers and Microsoft partners: direct versus indirect resellers, how partners earn money, what the new commerce experience changed, and when CSP beats an Enterprise Agreement.
